envelope.text: Takes `uint32_t` MILLISECONDS, not a `std::chrono::duration`, and returns

why:
RE-VERDICTED rename -> divergence 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5). The METHOD name does not differ at all — `nros::ActionClient<A>::wait_for_action_server(timeout_ms)` is the same word with the same meaning — so `rename` (ours is the one that should change) has no referent, and the row itself says 'the method needs no change'. What differs is the owning TYPE, and that is already ledgered: `cpp:ActionServer` records the one-namespace constraint (rclcpp_action gets its own namespace and can say `Client<ActionT>`; we ship only `nros`, where `Client` is the service client), `cpp:ActionClient` inherits from it, and our half of THIS pair reports `divergence*` inherited from those. This row is the theirs-only mirror and now carries the same verdict, so the pair reads consistently. The open TYPE-name question stays open and stays where it belongs, on `cpp:ActionServer`; no name is proposed here. See `cpp:ActionServer`. ORIGINAL ROW (verdict was `rename`): we HAVE this -- `nros::ActionClient<A>::wait_for_action_server(timeout_ms)`, same name, same meaning. It reports as theirs-only only because the owning type is spelled differently; rclcpp_action puts the action entities in their OWN namespace, so they can be called `Client<ActionT>` and `Server<ActionT>` beside `rclcpp::Client`. We ship one namespace, `nros`, where `Client` is already the service client -- so ours are `nros::ActionClient<A>` / `nros::ActionServer<A>` and every rclcpp_action member correlates as theirs-only even where we have it. Recorded so the pair is visible: the method needs no change, the TYPE name is the open question.

phase-428 (RFC-0089) — DISPOSITION, and the reason this row needed one is the flip itself. This row was `theirs-only` while our action client was called `nros::ActionClient<A>`; now that the definition lives in `rclcpp_action::Client<A>` the pair CORRESPONDS, so a ported file compiles and nothing says the contract differs. That is exactly the case RFC-0089 exists for, and it is the first thing the flip surfaced.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp_action::Client<ActionT>::wait_for_action_server(std::chrono::duration timeout = -1)` returns `bool`, blocks the calling thread on the graph guard condition, and a negative timeout waits forever.

OURS: `wait_for_action_server(uint32_t timeout_ms = 5000)` returns `nros::Result`. Three bounded differences, each forced. (1) MILLISECONDS, not `std::chrono` — `<chrono>` is a hosted header this surface cannot require (issue 0112/0332), and the same `uint32_t` millisecond spelling is used by every other blocking helper here. (2) `Result`, not `bool` — RFC-0018 forbids exceptions, so a timeout and a not-yet-initialised client have to be distinguishable by return code rather than by throw. (3) NO INFINITE WAIT: the timeout is unsigned and REQUIRED (see the correction below), because RFC-0021 requires a blocking helper to drive the executor and a wait that never returns starves every other entity on a single-threaded transport.

ADOPT-BOUNDED: the name and the meaning are upstream's, the units and the error channel are ours. A ported `client->wait_for_action_server()` is a `static_assert` refusal naming the budget (`NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT`), and a ported `wait_for_action_server(std::chrono::seconds(1))` does not compile either; both are loud.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ROW CORRECTED to the code. It said the timeout DEFAULTS to 5000 ms; phase-417 stage 3 removed that substitution, and `action_client.hpp` declares `wait_for_action_server(uint32_t timeout_ms)` with no default beside a no-argument overload that is a `static_assert` refusal. Sentences above are corrected in place. The envelope (milliseconds, `Result` rather than `bool`) is now stated on the method's doc comment; the required budget was already stated there and in the porting guide's table.

phase-488 (2026-10-21), measured on the stock ros2/examples ports in `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/rclcpp-examples/` (edit counts in its `edits.json`). `wait_for_action_server(std::chrono::duration)` ADDED on hosted builds (`NROS_CPP_HAS_STD_CHRONO`), the `Rate` precedent (`cpp:Rate::Rate`): the millisecond form is unchanged and the chrono overload converts and delegates -- rounded UP, clamped to `UINT32_MAX` ms -- so a ported `while (!client->wait_for_action_server(10s))` compiles (`Result`'s explicit `operator bool`). The refusal is NOT weakened: there is still no argument-free form, and a NEGATIVE duration (upstream's "forever") is refused at the call with `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT_RUNTIME`. Freestanding keeps the millisecond form only.
